criterion: M3 materials second stage: every run against evidence/m3-materials2-bounds.json, failures and abandoned attempts included

runs.what: exact Fresnel amplitudes for s and p at both interfaces, averaged, with the specification's Gaussian sensitivity
runs.result: fail: 0.0562 at cos 0.2 on base index 2.0 (bound 0.04), down from 0.26. Harmonics 8 against 24 made no difference; the rest came from the Gaussian sensitivity, a different fit to the colour matching functions than the reference integrates.

runs.what: the sensitivity tabulated from the reference's own colour matching fit (every 10 nm of optical path, 0 to 40,000 nm), white-balanced the same way; conductors (F0 above 0.25) keep the Schlick path until a complex-index reference exists
runs.result: pass: worst 0.0185 at cos 1 on base index 2.0; controls fail (Schlick interfaces 0.260, the specification's two harmonics 0.261).

runs.what: Beer-Lambert along each refracted direction's own path, thickness / |cos|, in eval; image lighting takes the view's refracted path
runs.result: pass: 1.1e-16 at 120 points; control (one attenuation for every direction) 0.276. Limit, stated plainly: the reference shares the model's interface, so this checks that the path length is applied, not the interface itself; an independent slab path tracer stays in not_covered_yet.

runs.what: attempt: base weight (1 - c E_o)(1 - c E_i) / (1 - c sqrt(E_o E_i)) for the peaked base, / (1 - c E_avg) for the smooth base
runs.result: fail: albedo 1.059 at grazing view (energy gained) on anisotropic bases. Abandoned.

runs.what: attempt: 1 - c max(E_o, E_i) for the peaked base, the smooth base as attempt 1
runs.result: fail: worst loss 0.070 (bound 0.02), and the energy test's conservation family exceeded 1 + 1e-3 at 36 points (smooth-base excess). Abandoned.

runs.what: probe, not kept: sqrt((1 - c E_o)(1 - c E_i))
attempt: 1 - c max(E_o, E_i) for everything the base reflects
runs.result: fail: worst loss 0.071; conservation exceeded 1 + 1e-3 at 4 points (worst 3.8e-3), all at view cosine 0.02 with coat roughness 0.05. A converged quadrature shows the cause: there the split-albedo table reads E 0.0037 below the coat lobe's true energy (the table's theta grid is coarse at grazing), and the old form's extra loss had hidden it. Reverted: the default coat stays as it was (loss up to 0.230), and the bound stays an open failure. Next: a sqrt(mu) axis for the A and B tables (as the sheen table has) and a tabulated coat-over-base compensation.

runs.what: test_pbr_energy --full, test_pbr_reciprocity, test_pbr_spec, test_lighting --full, and the material and lighting GPU parity on D3D12 WARP and WebGPU SwiftShader
runs.result: pass on every existing bound. Two tests were retargeted with reasons: the reciprocity test's spectral check now compares the series with the specification's interfaces (polarized = false) against the spectral reference with the same interfaces, which is what it measures; the spec-form test's expected value uses the text's Schlick interfaces. One process error of mine: the first GPU run used HLSL generated before my last WGSL edit and failed (ratio 943 on the volume family); after regenerating, both backends pass.

runs.what: method note 1: the reciprocal compensation lobe with hat tables, E_c read at the hat nodes; an anisotropic base reads the isotropic tables at alpha = sqrt(alpha_x alpha_y)
runs.result: fail: worst 0.095, albedo up to 1.077 (anisotropy 0.6). Isotropic points 0.9997 to 1.0056: E_c read at the nodes overstates the coat-weighted albedo Q by 2% to 7% (piecewise-linear interpolation of a convex curve), and the isotropic tables misrepresent anisotropic lobes.

runs.what: hat coefficients from the cosine-weighted least-squares projection of E_c (a table over coat roughness); anisotropic hat tables on the A4 grid, binned in the same VNDF samples as A4 and B4, with their hemispherical means
runs.result: fail on the excess only: worst |albedo - 1| 0.0169 (bound 0.02), albedo up to 1.0031 (bound 1 + 1e-3). Q now within 2.5e-3 of a quadrature reference. Every point over 1 + 1e-3 had the uncoated anisotropic base over it too (up to 1.0033).

runs.what: method note 2: anisotropic tables on u = sqrt(mu) and k^2 axes
runs.result: fail on the excess only: worst 0.0105, albedo up to 1.00265; the uncoated base reaches 1.00269 at the same points. The anisotropic furnace in test_pbr_energy improved from 3.35e-3 to 2.69e-3.

runs.what: method note 3: azimuth axis on sin^2(phi)
runs.result: rejected: the coat excess fell to 1.61e-3, but the table read 0.096 low at view cosine 0.08 and azimuth 77 degrees (the last sin^2 interval spans 68 to 90 degrees). Reverted to the uniform azimuth axis.

runs.what: the state after run 7 with run 8 reverted
runs.result: |albedo - 1| passes: worst 0.0105 against 0.02 (was 0.230). Open failure on the excess: albedo up to 1.00265 against 1 + 1e-3, at anisotropic points only, all inherited from the uncoated anisotropic base (1.00269 there), which meets its own furnace bound of 2e-2. The specExact control fails at 0.127.

runs.what: test_pbr_energy --full, test_pbr_reciprocity, test_pbr_spec, test_lighting --full, ctest 53 of 53, and the material and lighting GPU parity on D3D12 WARP and WebGPU SwiftShader
runs.result: pass. furnace_anisotropic worst 2.69e-3 (bound 2e-2); conservation worst 3.5e-4; reciprocity 3.75e-14 with the lobe in. GPU material parity: WARP 0.054 of the bound (was 0.62), SwiftShader 0.196; lighting shading WARP 0.47, SwiftShader 0.37. Cost: test_pbr_improve takes about 36 s alone and ctest about 48 s with 8 jobs (18 s before).

runs.what: gpu_pbr_parity and gpu_lighting_parity on the RTX 4090 under the GPU lock (04:56:37Z to 04:56:42Z), pinned 82e8d81
runs.result: pass: material parity 0.054 of the bound, 0 values outside, control fails; lighting shading 0.36, prefilter 0.0035, clusters 0 misses off the boundary.

runs.what: method note 4: the dense anisotropic table (32 x 16 x 48 x 12, 16,384 samples) generated once and embedded, hats on the old grid, the 768 x 384 rule at anisotropic points
runs.result: pass: |albedo - 1| worst 0.0112 (bound 0.02); excess worst 5.93e-04 (ceiling 1e-3) at view cosine 0.05, azimuth 45 degrees, coat 0.5, coat roughness 0.3, anisotropy 1.0, roughness 0.2. The specExact control fails at 0.1274. With the 384 x 192 rule on the same table the excess reads 1.23e-03, which the exploration traced to that rule's own 1.8e-3 error.

runs.what: pbr_aniso_gen wrote src/renderer/data/aniso_albedo.f32 (2,359,296 bytes, 11.6 s on 32 threads); test_pbr_aniso_table checks it
runs.result: pass: SHA-256 02d0431fab66a1ba0539f50d20d78cd4a68b6d49deb553e462bf0f2dfa961338 matches the committed file; 64 seeded entries regenerated, worst 2.93e-08 (bound 1e-6); controls fail as required (flipped bit changes the hash; 1,024 samples miss by 1.01e-03).

runs.what: ctest (59 of 59), test_pbr_energy --full, test_pbr_reciprocity, test_pbr_spec, test_lighting --full, and the material and lighting GPU parity on D3D12 WARP
runs.result: pass. furnace_anisotropic worst 9.31e-4 (bound 2e-2; was 2.69e-3); conservation worst 3.46e-4; reciprocity 3.75e-14. GPU material parity on WARP 0.0535 of the bound (was 0.054), control fails; lighting shading on WARP 0.47. The table buffer grows from 1,622,447 to 2,065,391 floats. Cost: test_pbr_improve takes about 31 s in ctest mode and about 2 minutes with --json.

runs.what: gpu_pbr_parity and gpu_lighting_parity on the RTX 4090 under the GPU lock (07:34:11Z to 07:34:16Z), pinned e70073e
runs.result: pass: material parity 0.0539 of the bound, control fails; lighting shading 0.36, prefilter 0.0035.

status: Second stage passes on the CPU: iridescence, volume path length and clearcoat energy, including the 1 + 1e-3 ceiling (excess 5.93e-04) since run clearcoat-9 (2026-10-12). GPU material parity passes on WARP and the RTX 4090.
